A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InverseBench work. All 29 pages, including Appendices A–C, are available and readable; text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments across five scientific inverse problems, including quantitative results in Appendix A and robustness and diagnostic analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 3–8 and the MRI pathology-detection evaluation in Table 10.

M1.justification: The benchmark framework, evaluated diffusion procedures and adaptations, and pretrained model architectures remain unchanged in Sections 2–4 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same five inverse problems, datasets, MRI generalization and pathology scenarios, and out-of-distribution source and prior tests.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 3–8 and 10. Both retain the same PnPDP methods and domain-specific baselines, including MRI end-to-end models and Navier–Stokes gradient-estimation variants.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, measurement settings, accuracy and efficiency metrics, training budgets, and tuning procedures are identical. The MRI diagnostic evaluation still uses 171 images from 14 volumes.

E4.justification: Both retain the same measurement-sparsity, initialization, PDE-stability, generalization, prior-mismatch, MRI diagnostic, and black-hole multimodality analyses. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including means and standard deviations over 94 MRI test cases and 10 FWI cases. Neither version adds run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 10 retains the E2E-VarNet and PnP-DM tie at mAP50 = 0.500; Figure 1 preserves the same plotted comparisons.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, assumptions, definitions, and derivations remain unchanged, including equations 1–23 and the ranking-score definition. No theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both claim the same benchmark contribution covering five scientific inverse problems and 14 representative PnPDP algorithms, with unchanged claims about their strengths, computational costs, and limitations.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning PDE stability, initialization, prior mismatch, exact forward models, inference speed, and multimodal posteriors are unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–C.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, model configurations in Table 11, hyperparameter searches and choices in Table 12, hardware information, and code/data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the algorithm taxonomy and domain-specific related-work discussions in Appendix B.

P1.justification: Figure 1 corrects 'vortocity' to 'vorticity' in two labels, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining wording, section organization, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 has small sizing and placement adjustments, corrected labels, and lower-resolution raster panels. Its content remains the same; other figures and tables retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific evidence, methodological documentation, claims, and limitations are unchanged throughout both PDFs. Figure 1 gains a spelling correction but loses some image sharpness through downsampling; its comparisons remain readable. These limited presentation changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
